# settlement-service

Node.js, no dependencies. `npm test` runs the suite.

Amounts are integer minor units (cents). Times are epoch milliseconds.

## Fees

`feeFor(amountMinor, plan)` returns `roundHalfEven(amountMinor * bps / 10000) + fixedMinor` for
the plan. Plans: `standard` (290 bps + 30), `growth` (250 bps + 25). Unknown plans throw
`unknown_plan`. `roundHalfEven(numerator, denominator)` is in `src/money.mjs`.

## Refunds

`new RefundBook(charges, ledger, clock)`, then `refund({merchantId, chargeId, amountMinor, idempotencyKey})`.

- Non-empty string ids and key and a positive safe-integer amount, otherwise `invalid_refund`.
- The charge must exist and belong to the merchant (`charge_not_found`) and be `captured`
  (`charge_not_captured`).
- Idempotency keys are scoped to the merchant. Reusing a key for the same merchant returns the
  original refund unchanged, even if the amount differs, without posting anything. The same key
  used by a different merchant is an independent request.
- The total refunded for a charge can never exceed its captured amount
  (`refund_exceeds_capture`).
- Each refund returns part of the charge fee: `floor(chargeFee * amountMinor / chargeAmount)`,
  except the refund that brings the charge to fully refunded, which returns exactly the fee not yet
  returned. Fully refunding a charge therefore always returns the whole fee.
- A refund is `{id, merchantId, chargeId, amountMinor, feeReturnMinor, currency, createdAt}`
  with ids `rf_1`, `rf_2`, ... and `createdAt` from the clock. It is posted to the ledger.
  Callers receive copies; mutating them does not affect the book.

## Ledger

`Ledger#postRefund(refund)` appends balanced lines `{account, amountMinor, currency, refundId}`:
`customer_refunds` +amount, `merchant:<merchantId>` -(amount - feeReturn) and `fees` -feeReturn.
Lines for a refund always sum to zero. `balance(account, currency)` sums an account.

## Settlement

`settle({charges, refunds, merchantId, from, to})` returns one row per currency, sorted by
currency code: `{currency, grossMinor, refundsMinor, feesMinor, netMinor, payoutMinor, carryoverMinor}`.

- Gross counts the merchant's `captured` charges with `capturedAt` in `[from, to)`. Pending
  and failed charges are never settled.
- Refunds count the merchant's refunds with `createdAt` in `[from, to)`.
- Fees are the fees of the counted charges minus `feeReturnMinor` of the counted refunds.
- `netMinor = grossMinor - refundsMinor - feesMinor`, `payoutMinor = netMinor`,
  `carryoverMinor = 0`.
- A currency with no counted charges or refunds has no row.

## Webhooks

`verifyWebhook({payload, timestamp, signature, secret, now, seen})`; `timestamp` and `now` are
epoch **seconds**; `seen` is a `Set` owned by the caller.

- The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `${timestamp}.${payload}` with the secret and
  must match exactly (compare in constant time) or the result is `{ok:false, reason:'bad_signature'}`.
- `|now - timestamp| > 300` gives `{ok:false, reason:'stale_timestamp'}`.
- A delivery whose `${timestamp}.${signature}` is already in `seen` gives
  `{ok:false, reason:'replayed'}`.
- Otherwise add it to `seen` and return `{ok:true}`. Checks run in the order signature,
  timestamp, replay.

input.body:
Fixed in commit ff3dd4f. It only changes src/webhooks.mjs and tests/webhooks.test.mjs, so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch.

- **Signature:** the full lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `${timestamp}.${payload}` is now compared in constant time with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Before, only the first 16 characters were compared. A signature that is the wrong length or not a string gets `bad_signature`.
- **Timestamp:** `timestamp` and `now` are treated as epoch seconds, and a delivery is rejected when `|now - timestamp| > 300`. Before, the code compared against 300_000 and only checked one direction, so a delivery replayed 20 minutes later still passed.
- **Replay:** accepted deliveries are now added to the caller's `seen` set. Before, nothing was ever added, so replays were never caught. Rejected deliveries are not recorded.
- Checks run in this order: signature, timestamp, replay.

Regression tests cover forging a signature by matching its prefix, truncated/extended/uppercase/non-string signatures, a different payload/timestamp/secret, the ±300s limits (including a 20-minute replay), replay detection and check order. All 7 webhook tests pass. The 4 other failing tests on main are PAY-31's, which I'm resuming now.

- **Signature:** the full lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `${timestamp}.${payload}` is now compared in constant time with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Before, only the first 16 characters were compared. A signature that is the wrong length or not a string gets `bad_signature`.
- **Timestamp:** `timestamp` and `now` are treated as epoch seconds, and a delivery is rejected when `|now - timestamp| > 300`. Before, the code compared against 300_000 and only checked one direction, so a delivery replayed 20 minutes later still passed.
- **Replay:** accepted deliveries are now added to the caller's `seen` set. Before, nothing was ever added, so replays were never caught. Rejected deliveries are not recorded.
- Checks run in this order: signature, timestamp, replay.

Regression tests cover forging a signature by matching its prefix, truncated/extended/uppercase/non-string signatures, a different payload/timestamp/secret, the ±300s limits (including a 20-minute replay), replay detection and check order. All 7 webhook tests pass. The 4 other failing tests on main are PAY-31's, which I'm resuming now."}}

input.body:
Fixed in commit e870212. All 30 tests pass. When I ran the new regression tests against the original code, 15 of them failed.

**What caused finance's reports to be off**
- **Refunded for more than was captured:** the capture limit only looked at the *last* refund on a charge, not the total of all of them. It now uses the total. Idempotency keys are also now scoped per merchant; before, one merchant's key could return another merchant's refund.
- **Payouts including money we never captured:** settlement skipped only `failed` charges, so `pending` charges were paid out. Now only `captured` charges count. Settlement also put every currency into one row under the first currency it saw; it now returns one row per currency, sorted by code.
- **Balances off by small amounts:**
  - Fees rounded half-up (`Math.round`) instead of half-to-even.
  - Fully refunding a charge could leave a cent or two of the fee unreturned. The refund that finishes a charge now returns exactly what's left of the fee.
  - The ledger took the full refund amount out of the merchant's balance instead of `amount - feeReturn`, so each refund's lines didn't add up to zero.

**Changes to requirements (from Maya)**
- `refund_window_expired`: a refund more than 30 days after `capturedAt` is rejected; exactly 30 days is allowed. The check runs after idempotent replay and before the capture limit.
- `payoutMinor = max(netMinor, 0)`, and any shortfall is reported as a positive `carryoverMinor`. `netMinor` is unchanged.
- I added both rules to the README so it matches the code.

Public interfaces are unchanged. Note that fee rounding stays half-to-even, as the README specifies.

content.text:
I fixed and committed two tickets, each in its own commit: the urgent SEC-7 webhook incident and PAY-31, the settlement reports finance couldn't reconcile. All 30 tests pass and both tickets are marked done.

**SEC-7 (commit `ff3dd4f`)**
Priya assigned this production security incident while I was partway through PAY-31. My PAY-31 fixes were finished but had no tests yet, so I set that work aside and paused the ticket. This commit only touches the webhook code and its tests, so it can be copied onto the release branch by itself. Three problems in `src/webhooks.mjs` are fixed:
- **Signature check:** only the first 16 characters of the signature were compared. It now compares the whole signature, in constant time.
- **Timestamp check:** it treated seconds as milliseconds and only checked one direction, so a delivery replayed 20 minutes later still passed. It now rejects anything more than 300 seconds off either way.
- **Replay check:** accepted deliveries were never recorded, so a replay was never caught. They're recorded now.

**PAY-31 (commit `e870212`)**
- **Refunded for more than was captured:** the limit only counted the last refund on a charge instead of all of them. Refund keys weren't separated by merchant, so one merchant's key could return another merchant's refund.
- **Payouts with money we never captured:** settlement paid out pending charges, and it lumped every currency into one row.
- **Balances off by small amounts:**
  - Fees rounded half-up instead of half-to-even.
  - Fully refunding a charge didn't always return the whole fee.
  - The ledger took the whole refund out of the merchant's balance, including the returned fee, so each refund's entries didn't add up to zero.
- **Maya's two changes to the requirements:**
  - Refunds more than 30 days after capture are rejected.
  - Payouts can't go below 0; any shortfall is reported as a carryover amount.

  I also added both rules to the README, since they weren't there yet.
- **Tests:** I added regression tests for all of the above, including a new ledger test file. When I ran the new tests against the original code, 15 failed.

I posted in #payments-eng to tell Priya the incident fix is ready to copy to the release branch. In the same message I answered Dev, who suggested switching fee rounding to half-up: I kept half-to-even because the README requires it, and changing it would be Maya's call.
